items.title: Google open-sources ML Drift, the GPU engine behind LiteRT — and ships it with a guide for coding agents to write their own shaders
items.summary: ML Drift is the cross-platform GPU compute engine (OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU) that powers on-device inference in LiteRT, now open-sourced under Apache 2.0 and usable standalone. It succeeds the old TFLite GPU delegate, adds 5D tensor support and prefill/decode-aware kernels for on-device LLMs, and previews a desktop WebGPU backend for Windows and Linux.
items.why: The GPU engine itself is edge/mobile infra, but the real hook is that Google shipped an agentic SKILL.md guide alongside it so a coding agent can safely author, register, and verify its own custom GPU shaders — a pattern worth stealing anywhere you want an agent to touch risky, low-level code.
items.action: Skim the SKILL.md in google-ai-edge/ml-drift to see exactly how they scope what an agent is allowed to generate and verify for shader code — a reusable template for giving an agent safe write-access to a tricky part of your own stack.

eval.reason: Genuine new open-source release succeeding the legacy TFLite GPU delegate, with concrete new capabilities; not a duplicate of anything sent previously.
Re-fetched the post fresh; loads and matches, dated Oct 8 2026.
